# Unslop UI Design Instructions

Use these instructions whenever creating, reviewing, polishing, or redesigning a user interface. Apply the Unslop methodology: remove generic AI-looking decoration, preserve the product and its information architecture, and make the result feel specific to this product.

Adapted from [Unslop by Damir Sokolovsky (@heydamir)](https://github.com/heydamir/unslop), licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Keep this attribution in copies and adaptations.

## Principles

- Keep the product name, real brand assets, features, content, and section order. Do not invent capabilities, claims, or data. You may replace meaningless placeholders with plausible content.
- Remove slop without replacing it with another trend. Do not default to glass, grain, noise, neon, bento grids, or a generic “modern” template.
- Quiet the chrome. Keep navigation, controls, borders, and text within a coherent tinted-neutral ramp and use one restrained accent.
- Concentrate richness in one or two meaningful moments: a carefully rendered product object, a chart whose colors encode data, or a visual from the product’s world. Every color and detail in those moments must mean something.
- The result must be identifiable as this product without its logo. Derive decisions from what it does and who it serves, never from current trends.
- Do not change a good screen merely to make it different. If the screen has no slop, report that and suggest no more than three refinements with exact values; implement them only when asked.

## Workflow

1. **Inspect the rendered screen.** Find the implementation and its existing design system. Run the app or open the page and take a screenshot when practical; judge what users see, not code alone. For a live URL without source, make and work on a local copy. For a screenshot-only input, first recreate it as a static page and use that as the baseline. State clearly when the redesign is a handoff implementation rather than a change to the live site.
2. **Audit before editing.** Review every applicable group in the Audit checklist below. Record each issue as one concise line with its location and intended fix. For Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Hebrew, or any `dir="rtl"` screen, read the RTL rules below first; they override conflicting guidance.
3. **Choose scope honestly.**
   - Heavy slop across multiple groups: use all nine passes.
   - Light slop: fix only the audited issues and preserve the existing brand, palette, typography, layout, and visual direction. Put larger ideas in the report as suggestions.
   - No slop: report that plainly and stop after at most three optional, exact-value suggestions unless the user approves changes.
4. **Set a five-line direction before changes.** Base it on the product and its audience:
   - **Product:** what it does and for whom, in one plain sentence.
   - **Character:** two or three concrete adjectives. Avoid generic labels such as “clean,” “modern,” “sleek,” “minimal,” and “premium.”
   - **World:** a natural place or material that informs the neutral tint, accent, and visual.
   - **Moments:** one or two product-relevant places for rich color, material, and detail.
   - **Signature:** one small, repeatable detail that belongs to this product.
   Keep genuine branding that is not itself slop. If the user has asked to implement the redesign, proceed with the stated direction; otherwise show the audit and direction and wait for confirmation before editing.
5. **Apply the nine passes in order.** Finish each pass across the whole screen before starting the next. If most of the screen is being rebuilt, plan the passes first, then implement in one coherent change while still applying each pass in order. Spacing comes first; copy precedes type and layout; visuals and motion come last.
6. **Verify.** Render again when practical (no more than three screen renders per run), compare against the original and audit, and fix any remaining checklist issues. Run relevant project checks.
7. **Report.** Summarize the direction, the audit and changes by pass, verification performed, unresolved issues, and any image prompt written.

## Nine-pass redline workflow

1. **Spacing:** Put margins, padding, gaps, and fixed heights on the 4px grid (multiples of 4; 2px nudges only inside small controls; odd values only when needed for exact centering). Make like elements equal in size, padding, and gap; make within-group spacing smaller than between-group spacing; align icons, labels, and numbers to consistent columns. Typical padding is 16px for dense panels, 20–24px for cards, and 24–32px at page edges. Navigation rows are 32–36px high with 2–4px between rows; place a section label about 24px from the previous group and 8px from its own items. Remove arbitrary one-off values.
2. **Color:** Build backgrounds, surfaces, hairlines, and text from one low-saturation neutral ramp tinted to the product’s world. Apps and dashboards stay neutral; landing pages may use more world tint. Define primary, secondary, and muted text roles only. Use one accent sparingly for the primary action, selection, or one key figure. Rich color is reserved for meaningful moments and data. Preserve real brand color as the accent, not as a reason to color every surface. Semantic colors only signal meaning. Remove hue-to-hue gradients, gradient text, glows, colored shadows, radial washes, blobs, and neon borders. Hairlines use 6–10% opacity of the ramp’s text color. Dark depth comes from surface steps and hairlines; light shadows are soft and neutral. A subtle gradient may shift between tones of the same neutral only.
3. **Icons:** Replace emoji used as icons or label decoration with one existing project icon set, or Lucide if none exists. Use one size (16 or 18px), one 1.5px stroke, and the color of the icon’s text role. Give icons equal-width boxes and fixed 8–10px label gaps. Remove decorative icons; use a small status dot only when category color conveys meaning.
4. **Copy:** Write specific, factual headlines that say what the product does for whom. Do not invent facts. Remove greeting headlines, exclamation marks, hype, and vague claims. Keep labels short (e.g. “Search”), say what a comparison is against (e.g. “+12% vs last month”), and omit trailing periods from headlines, subheads, labels, buttons, and captions; normal multi-sentence paragraphs keep punctuation. Ask whether unverifiable claims are true; otherwise remove them and note them in the report. Use plausible names and values, never `[X]` or obviously fake data. Remove badges such as `PRO`, `New ✨`, or `Beta 🚀` unless genuinely needed, then make them quiet text.
5. **Type:** Choose a typeface for the direction; preserve a real brand face. Use one interface family plus at most one partner (mono for figures/meta or display face for large headlines). Prefer weights 400 and 500, with 600 only for rare emphasis; no 700–900 headings. Establish hierarchy with size and color, use sentence case, and avoid italic emphasis. Do not use negative letter spacing on small text; tighter tracking is only for large display text. Use tabular figures and one number format across the screen.
6. **Layout:** Preserve all features, content, and section order, but improve alignment and proportions. An app fills the viewport: use a 240–280px sidebar with fluid content, 24–32px page padding, and a content maximum around 1440–1600px. Do not squeeze an app into a narrow centered column. A windowed design remains visibly windowed. For a hero, prefer a meaningful full-width scene with text on calm open space and the product rising from below; otherwise use an asymmetric split or large product preview. Keep long headlines left-aligned; center only one or two short lines. Use one primary action and at most one secondary action. Keep navigation quiet. Compose the first screen without a dead empty band. On mobile, stack in reading order, simplify dense previews rather than shrinking them, and keep preview text at least 11px.
7. **Details:** Use radius by scale: small tags/keycaps/buttons 4–6px, controls/rows 8–10px, cards 12–16px, panels 14–20px. An inner radius equals the outer radius minus intervening padding, never below 4px; do not make everything a pill. Render counts/meta quietly; shortcuts as keycaps. Give charts a muted grid and mono labels, a clear hierarchy, and an appropriate chart type (trend=line, comparison=bars, share=stacked bar/list, goal=progress). Use one accent per chart; use several hues only when each represents a necessary series. Do not fill stats with decorative sparklines, mini-bars, or icons. Vary card sizes and pair one main chart with a smaller, different data view. Make active, hover, keyboard focus, and table states distinct but palette-consistent; show a visible focus ring. Keep button radii consistent. Use the signature detail only where it belongs.
8. **Visuals:** Remove decorative filler. Landing heroes need a truthful, product-relevant visual; dashboards and app screens usually need no generated image. Build a product preview in code using existing components and plausible data, centered on the one moment that proves the page’s promise. Use generated images only for a hero, empty state, onboarding, marketing, or when requested. Before the visual pass, consult the source’s [visual guidance](https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/blob/main/skills/unslop/references/visuals.md), [finished references](https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/blob/main/skills/unslop/references/refs.md), and, if using image treatments, [effects](https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/blob/main/skills/unslop/references/effects.md). Borrow composition, restraint, and craft—not another product’s subject, palette, or layout. Never use generic AI imagery (glossy blobs/orbs, nebulae, floating cubes, neon circuits, holograms, robots, glowing brains) unless it is literally relevant. If image generation is available, show the user the prompt, model, and size and ask before generating because it may incur cost. Use one clear physical subject, match lighting and edges to the page, exclude text/logos/UI/watermarks, save the asset in the project, provide meaningful alt text, and keep it static or subtly animated. Without a generation tool, build what is feasible, report the prompt, and do not ship a labeled placeholder.
9. **Motion:** Remove pointless loops, shimmer, breathing glows, floating elements, parallax, bouncy springs, `transition-all`, and card hover scaling. Keep only motion that explains feedback or state: quick color/surface changes, a tiny press scale-down, and short menu fade/rise. Use one easing curve (`cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`) and durations from the scale below. Transition only color, background, border, opacity, and transform; never animate layout dimensions/positions, margins, or large blurs. At most one restrained entrance: a short fade/rise with a small stagger.

## Spacing, layout, and visual tokens

These are starting points, not a mandate to replace a sound existing system. Keep a good project scale and fix how it is used.

- **Spacing scale:** `4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128px`. Controls: 4–12px internal spacing. Related rows: 2–8px. Groups: 12–24px. App sections: 32–64px; landing sections: 80–128px. Row heights: 32px compact, 36px default, 40–44px touch. Hero gap from nav to headline: 96–128px desktop, 48–64px mobile.
- **App shell:** sidebar 240–280px; page padding 24–32px; content max-width about 1440–1600px; top bar 56–64px. Navigation rows 32–36px with 2–4px gaps. Desktop stat cards share a height; use three or four compact stats per row. Main chart spans at least two-thirds of content and is 280–360px tall; pair it with a narrower list/table, not another same-sized chart.
- **Neutral ramps:** choose one graphite, warm, or ink family, or a similarly low-saturation tint. Dark ramp starting points (deepest/page/card/raised): graphite `#0f0f10/#141415/#19191b/#232325`; warm `#12110f/#161513/#1c1a18/#262421`; ink `#07080d/#0b0d14/#11141c/#1a1e28`. Light starting points (page/card/raised): graphite `#fafafa/#ffffff/#f4f4f5`; warm `#f7f4ee/#fdfbf7/#efe9df`; ink `#f5f7fa/#ffffff/#eceff4`. Hairlines are text color at about 8% opacity. Text roles should remain near the chosen ramp; muted text is for meta/captions and must still reach about 4.5:1 contrast.
- **Text colors:** dark graphite primary/secondary/muted `#ededed/#a1a1a6/#85858b`; dark warm `#efe9de/#aaa398/#8a847a`; dark ink `#eef0f5/#a3a9b8/#7a8296`. Light graphite `#171717/#525252/#737373`; light warm `#1f1b16/#5e554a/#7b7266`; light ink `#111827/#4b5565/#6b7487`.
- **Accents and semantics:** keep a real brand hue as the accent. Otherwise choose from the world: amber/coral/ember for warm, cobalt/teal/sky for cool, moss/sage for natural. Avoid purple-blue unless it is truly the brand. Accent occupies only a few percent of the screen. Text on/using an accent must reach 4.5:1 contrast; darken the accent or use dark text as needed. Semantic green starts at `#4cc38a` dark / `#16a34a` light; red at `#e5484d` dark / `#dc2626` light.
- **Buttons:** hero height 44–48px, navigation controls 32–36px, horizontal padding 16–20px. Use off-white with dark text or accent for dark-theme primary; primary text fill with white text or accent for light-theme primary. Secondary controls use raised surface, hairline, and primary text. A restrained inset top highlight on a dark button is acceptable; no glow.
- **Type scale:** labels/meta/counts 12/16px; captions 13–14/20px; body/nav 14–15/20–22px; wordmark 16–18px; hero subhead 18–20/28–30px, secondary color and max width about 36rem; card figures 28–32px; page title 28–36px/1.15; hero headline 56–72px desktop and 36–44px mobile, line-height 1.02–1.08. Keep letter spacing 0 below 16px; slightly positive tracking is acceptable for small muted Latin text; only large display type may be slightly negative. Display serif belongs only in large headlines.
- **Depth, radius, motion:** dark depth uses surface steps/hairlines; light small shadow `0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.05)` and floating shadow `0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.06)`. Use a consistent ease `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`: hover/press/toggles 120–180ms, menus 160–220ms, entrances/layout changes 300–500ms, stagger 40–60ms for at most six items. Entrances rise 6–12px; press scale 0.97–0.98.
- **Icons:** Lucide if no project set exists, 16 or 18px, 1.5px stroke, secondary or muted role color, and 8–10px label gap.

## Audit checklist: signs and required fixes

Report each finding with its location and fix. Cover every applicable group; do not merely say “polish UI.”

- **Surfaces/color:** purple-blue or violet-pink gradients on backgrounds/cards/buttons/nav → neutral surface and meaningful accent; gradient text → solid primary text; colored glows, emoji drop-shadows, glowing pills, radial washes, blurred blobs → remove and use surface steps/hairlines; neon borders → 6–10% hairlines; many near-identical text tints → three roles from one ramp; everything highlighted → one accent once or twice; glass cards with inner white highlight/colored shadow → plain raised surface and hairline.
- **Typography:** 800/900 headings → 400–500; uppercase tracked labels → sentence case with normal/slightly open tracking; too many sizes/weights → a small scale and primarily 400/500; inconsistent number formats → one format and tabular figures; negative tracking on small text → zero or slightly positive; italic emphasis → use color or weight.
- **Icons:** emoji navigation/labels/status/counts → one line-icon set or nothing; mixed icon sizes/colors → one size, stroke, and text-role color; icons drifting off column → equal-width boxes; sparkle for generic AI → remove or use a relevant plain icon only.
- **Spacing:** arbitrary values (e.g. 13px, 7px, 31px) → 4px scale; inconsistent list row height/gaps and sibling padding → equalize; groups closer to neighbors than to their own items → tighten internal gaps and widen group gaps; empty bands/cramped sections → balance the rhythm.
- **Copy:** greeting title → page/context title; exclamation marks → plain statement; unsupported deltas → name the comparison; wordy placeholders → short labels; hype/buzzwords → describe the actual behavior; trailing periods on short strings → remove; fake data → plausible values; unverifiable social/performance claims → confirm or remove.
- **Components/data:** glowing count/plan/shortcut/status pills → quiet mono text or keycaps; ubiquitous `PRO`, `New ✨`, `Beta 🚀` → remove or keep one necessary quiet badge; everything pill-shaped → radius by scale and nested-radius math; rainbow/glowing/pill-shaped charts or uppercase day labels → muted grid, mono labels, meaningful series and a highlight; multiple accent shades competing → neutral series with one highlighted datum; decorative mini-charts in every stat → label, figure, and comparison only; identical chart cards → one primary chart plus compact stats and a different secondary data view; gradient/sparkle logo → text wordmark and simple flat mark; glossy orb/glowing logo dot → flat single-color mark or wordmark.
- **Landing/hero:** decorative announcement badge → remove or use quiet factual link; generic headline such as “Supercharge your workflow with AI” → specific factual promise; headline gradient/shimmer → solid type; floating blobs/orbs/grids/glowing lines → simple background or real product visual; centered stack of everything → asymmetric split or text over a large product view, except a short hero with no visual; more than two hero actions or piled chips/avatars → one primary and at most one secondary; unsourced trust claims/stars/avatars → verify then make specific and quiet or remove; parallax/floating scroll elements → static composition; generic emoji feature cards → fewer cards with concrete copy and line icons or none.
- **Visuals:** blobs/orbs/liquid chrome/nebulas → product or concrete metaphor; stock robot/brain/circuit imagery for generic AI → remove or show the actual output; text/buttons/logos baked into image → real HTML text over clean artwork; image with mismatched hard edge/background → match page color or mask softly; imagery in every section → one useful visual, usually hero only.
- **Motion:** pulse/ping on non-live elements → static; `transition-all` and hover scaling → named color/surface transitions and tiny press-scale only; bounce/overshoot → one ease-out; everything entering from different directions → one short fade/rise with small stagger; parallax/floating loops → static; width/height/top/left animation → transform/opacity only.
- **Template fallback:** generic pure-grey/Inter/white/old-brand-button regardless of product world → tint neutrals to the product; a name-swappable headline → use product-specific nouns; empty or generic hero image → build a truthful product preview or world-specific image; same layout/type/palette for every product → let the direction decide.

## Banned buzzwords and claims

Do not use these as empty UI marketing language: **supercharge, seamless, unlock, magic, revolutionize, game-changing, AI-powered** (as a generic claim), or similar unsupported hype. Replace them with concrete, verifiable descriptions of what the product does. Avoid unsourced claims such as “Loved by 10,000+ teams” and “10x faster”; verify with the user or remove them.

## Right-to-left screens

For Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Hebrew, or any RTL screen, these rules take precedence:

- Set the root language and direction (`lang` and `dir="rtl"`). Use logical CSS/Tailwind properties (`margin-inline-*`, `padding-inline-*`, `inset-inline-*`, `text-align: start`; `ms-*`, `me-*`, `ps-*`, `pe-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`, `text-start`). Avoid hard-coded left/right and `ml-*`/`mr-*`.
- Mirror the layout: sidebar/logo on the right, primary action first from the right, progress fills right-to-left. Flip only directional icons (arrows, chevrons, undo/redo, reply/send, indent, sidebar toggle); never mirror objects, media controls, logos, or Latin-letter icons. Do not `scaleX(-1)` an entire container.
- Isolate Latin, numbers, code, email, URLs, links, user-entered content, and signed values with `<bdi>` or `unicode-bidi: isolate`; use `<bdi dir="ltr">` for signed values. Email/URL/phone/code inputs stay LTR but align to the end. Use `dir="auto"` only on inline content.
- Use one digit system for the screen; format with `Intl.NumberFormat` and use tabular figures.
- Choose a font designed for the script with real weights and a compatible Latin partner. Options include IBM Plex Sans Arabic, Noto Sans Arabic, Readex Pro, Vazirmatn, Noto Sans Hebrew/Heebo/Rubik, and Noto Nastaliq Urdu. Preserve real brand choices; do not default blindly to Cairo/Tajawal. Arabic letter spacing is always zero, with no fake italic or bold. Use body 15–17px (captions at least 13px), line-height 1.6–1.8 body and 1.3–1.4 headings. Do not justify short UI text or use tatweel for spacing.
- Use Arabic comma `،`, semicolon `؛`, and question mark `؟`; no spaces before punctuation. Keep copy in one natural register, with short labels, no greetings, exclamation marks, generic hype, or periods on short labels/buttons. Verify quoted scripture/poetry exactly with a user-named source; never invent or paraphrase it, and style it plainly in a reading face without glow, gradient, outline, or animation.

## Optional image effects

Use glyph rendering, halftone, dithering, or duotone only on the main visual, only when it fits the direction, and never as general decoration. Read pixels once, never inside an animation loop; precompute reusable glyphs/cells; animate at 8–12 steps/second with only a small fraction changing; pause offscreen; cap canvas device-pixel ratio at 2.

## Final checklist

- [ ] Direction is written and every pass follows it; screen still belongs uniquely to the product.
- [ ] All audited findings are fixed or explicitly reported as unresolved.
- [ ] Spacing follows the 4px rhythm and repeated elements align and match.
- [ ] One tinted neutral ramp, three text roles, and a contrast-safe accent; no hue gradients, gradient text, glows, colored shadows, or blobs.
- [ ] No decorative emoji; one icon set, size, stroke, color role, and alignment.
- [ ] Type fits the character; weights 400–600, sentence case, no small negative tracking, no italic emphasis.
- [ ] Copy has no hype, exclamation, greeting headline, trailing punctuation on short strings, or unverified claim.
- [ ] Numbers use one format and tabular figures; data is plausible.
- [ ] RTL follows all direction, mirroring, bidi, font, and digit rules where applicable.
- [ ] Nested radii add up; buttons fit the component style; table header/value/selection/focus states are distinct.
- [ ] Hero has a real visual/product preview and at least one meaningful moment, never a generic filler image or labeled placeholder.
- [ ] First screen has no dead empty band; mobile layout is readable and simplified.
- [ ] Motion is purposeful, non-bouncy, non-looping unless it represents live status, and does not animate layout properties.
- [ ] Replacing the product name with another product would not leave the screen equally plausible.

## Optional shareable redline story

Create a story/video only when requested. Use a standalone copy at `unslop-story/story.html`; preserve the original as step 0. Use 3–5 cumulative CSS steps that tween values rather than changing structure. Add only a few well-chosen redline measurements, limit text swaps to eight, reserve space for entering elements, and crop tightly on the most visible change. The final shipping implementation remains ordinary project code without story-only classes/attributes. Credit any video `unslop by @heydamir`.
